blocks.text: Elements can be classified by the subshell that holds their valence electrons. The valence electrons of the elements of the first two groups are in s subshells, so these elements form the s block. The transition elements belong to the d block, and the two series at the bottom of the table, the lanthanides and actinides, are the f block. The remaining elements, groups 13 to 18 including the inert gases of the last group, belong to the p block.

Knowing an element's block gives valuable information about its characteristics: chemical reactivity, oxidation states and other properties such as electronegativity, ionization energy and electron filling.

blocks.prompt: Element X is in group 2 and element Y in group 15. Name the block of each and the subshell its valence electrons occupy.
blocks.explanation: X is in the s block, with its valence electrons in an s subshell; Y is in the p block, with its valence electrons in a p subshell.

items: s block: groups 1 and 2; p block: groups 13 to 18; d block: transition elements; f block: lanthanides and actinides.
The block tells you about reactivity, oxidation states, electronegativity, ionization energy and electron filling.
